about: Earlier names allowed in the repository, where, and why. Read by scripts/check_names.py; explained in docs/kept-names.md. kind: contract = a name another program we do not build expects; data = a value already stored or deployed; fallback = an earlier name still read so old installs and deployments keep working; record = a statement of origin that must name it; phase-6 = our own code names, renamed in the next step and removed from this list then.

rules.reason: The app's notice states where the window and shell come from and who made them.
The website's demo is the app's window: the upstream compiled renderer, patched. Its internal identifiers are the upstream bytes.
The upstream app's own dependency list (@anysphere/* packages) that the pinned renderer and shell were built with; the identity fields are Simeon's.
Bootstrap reads the upstream 0.18.0 app by its real name and download address (Grok Bot.app, Grok_Bot_0.18.0.dmg).
The window patch finds the upstream strings (Grok Bot, New Bot, Caisra, the .sand-grok-bot-mark class) to replace them, and its tests feed it those strings.
The packager renames the upstream shell's executable and helper bundles, which are named Grok Bot, to Simeon.
The packager recognises the upstream maker's names in Info.plist strings in order to replace them.
Generated protocol code: service, message and field names the pinned window and the server speak on the wire (aiserver.v1.GrokBotService, Xai* messages).
The server answers the Connect service aiserver.v1.GrokBotService and the GROK_BOT source enum the app sends.
Settings are read as SIMEON_<NAME> and the earlier CLAIDOR_<NAME> is still read, so deployments keep working while their variables are renamed.
Sessions, tokens, custom-domain records, placeholder e-mails and webhook headers made before the rename carry the earlier name and are still accepted (or still sent).
The data folder was ~/.caisra (with a .grokbot-data-root-v1 marker); the first start moves it to ~/.simeon, and the earlier folder stays protected from the local-exec daemon.
A testing Docker box made before the rename carries the earlier owner label and is still recognised, so it is replaced cleanly.
The app's sign-in callback scheme was caisra:// before simeon://; a build from before the rename can still finish a sign-in.
Meter event names and Composio user ids already stored under the earlier name.
A real S3 bucket that serves images; renaming it means moving the files first.
A published npm package (@spaire/sdk) the checkout imports; its name is not ours to change.

Database migrations are the history of the live schema: table and column names they created (court_decisions.ohadata_code, the tie-out tables) exist in the database, and a past migration's text is not rewritten.

The Render blueprint keeps the service names, the CLAIDOR_ variable keys and the repository address that exist on Render until they are changed there (a renamed service in the blueprint would be a new, empty service).

Values the app and the box send or read: the cloud computer's Docker owner label, the cloud-agent source value "grok-bot", the model provider id "claidor", and desktop file names. Renamed together with the app's side, with the earlier value still accepted.

The Mac app's own code names, comments and file names that still carry an earlier name (the provider id "claidor", GrokBot*/Anysphere* types, @anysphere logger names, [claidor] test fixtures). Phase 6 renames them and removes this rule; strings a person can see are already Simeon's.
